items.passage: In a 2019 study, a team led by mathematician Chad M. Topaz combined the online catalogs of 18 major US art museums with tens of thousands of judgments from crowdsourced workers to estimate the gender and ethnicity of the artists in each collection. Several of the museums differed sharply from the rest. At the High Museum of Art in Atlanta, for example, the estimated share of artists who are Black or African American is ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?

table.title: Estimated Shares of Women and of Black Artists in Five Museum Collections
columns: Artists who are Black or African American (%)
rows: Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles

items.explanation: The text asks for the estimated share of artists in the High Museum of Art’s collection who are Black or African American. In the table, the High Museum of Art row shows 10.6 in the column for Black or African American artists, so choice B completes the text.

A.why_wrong: 2.7% is the estimated share of Black or African American artists at the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles, not at the High Museum of Art.

C.why_wrong: 24.9% is the estimated share of women artists at the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles.

D.why_wrong: 10.7% is the High Museum of Art’s estimated share of artists who are women, not its share of Black or African American artists.

sources.what: Topaz et al. 2019, PLoS One 14(3): e0212852: public online catalogs of 18 major US museums scraped, about 10,000 artist records sent to crowdsourcing (Amazon Mechanical Turk), 45,000 responses; gender and ethnicity inferred; outlier museums identified (HMA stands out for Black/African American artists)
Table 2 estimates: DIA women 7.4, Black 1.6; HMA 10.7, 10.6; MFAH 16.1, 1.1; MOCA (Los Angeles) 24.9, 2.7; WMAA 22.1, 2.3; museum names from Table 1 footnote
Chad Topaz affiliation: Department of Mathematics and Statistics, Williams College (author list of the paper)
High Museum of Art is in Atlanta, Georgia

items.notes: Percentages are the paper's observed estimates (Table 2), which come with confidence intervals; the passage says 'estimated'. Subject replaced: national parks lookup (judge tell: clone of the official lookup format with tourist filler).

fixes: 'mathematician Chad M. Topaz and his colleagues' changed to 'a team led by mathematician Chad M. Topaz' ('and colleagues' framing was in 14 of 21 items of this file)

items.rewrite: New subject (Topaz 2019 artist demographics in US museum collections) replacing national-park acreage; research framing instead of 'a student writing a report', wrong-column distractor added.

items.passage: For its 2021 Digital News Report, the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism analyzed a YouGov survey of more than 92,000 online news consumers in 46 markets. The researchers documented a widening gap between respondents’ trust in news generally and their trust in news encountered through intermediaries such as search engines and social media platforms. In Finland, for example, 65 percent of respondents trusted news overall, but only ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 37 percent trusted news found on social media.
21 percent trusted news found on social media.
18 percent trusted news found on social media.
31 percent trusted news found on social media.

table.title: Trust in News among Online Survey Respondents in Three Markets, 2021
rows: Trust in news on social media

items.explanation: The text needs Finland’s level of trust in news found on social media, set against its 65 percent trust in news overall. In the table’s row for trust in news on social media, the value in the Finland column is 18, so only 18 percent of respondents in Finland trusted news found on social media, which illustrates the gap the researchers documented.

A.why_wrong: 37 percent is Peru’s value for trust in news on social media; in Finland, that value is 18 percent.

B.why_wrong: 21 percent is Taiwan’s value for trust in news on social media; in Finland, that value is 18 percent.

D.why_wrong: 31 percent is the share of respondents in Taiwan who trusted news overall, not Finland’s trust in news on social media, which was 18 percent.

sources.what: Digital News Report 2021 is based on a YouGov survey of over 92,000 online news consumers in 46 markets
trust gap between news in general and news found in aggregated environments (search and social media) has grown
Finland: trust in news overall 65%, trust in news on social media 18%
Peru: trust in news overall 40%, trust in news on social media 37%
Taiwan: trust in news overall 31%, trust in news on social media 21%

items.notes: Survey fieldwork January to February 2021 (online questionnaire by YouGov). Subject replaced: ILO 2024 labor force estimates (judge tell: 2024 data postdate the bank; bare lookup).

fixes: last sentence and options rebuilt: 'According to the table, news on social media was trusted by ______' with 'N percent of respondents in X' options copied the skeleton of official 2.41; now 'the table shows that trust in news found on social media stood at ______' with 'N percent in X' options

after blind round 2: the key (Peru, 37 vs 40 overall) did not illustrate the documented gap; the last sentence now sets Finland’s 65 percent overall against the blank, key 18 percent (Finland, social media), distractors two misplaced values and one wrong row

items.passage: Many medieval stories survive only because a single manuscript escaped fire, decay, or reuse. To estimate how much was lost, Mike Kestemont and Folgert Karsdorp led a team that borrowed statistical methods ecologists use to gauge how many species in a habitat have gone undetected. They applied these methods to chivalric and heroic stories, such as tales of King Arthur, written in six languages. Of the six, the language whose works had the lowest estimated rate of survival was ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: Dutch.
Icelandic.
French.
English.

figure.title: Estimated Survival of Medieval Chivalric and Heroic Works, by Language
figure.y_axis: Estimated share of works that survive (%)
figure.description: One bar per language; y-axis 0 to 100 in steps of 10. Dutch about 49, English about 39, French about 54, German about 79, Icelandic about 77, Irish about 81. English is the shortest bar, about 10 points below Dutch.

data.series: Estimated share of works that survive (%)

items.explanation: The graph’s shortest bar belongs to English: an estimated 39% of English chivalric and heroic works survive, lower than any other language shown. So choice D completes the statement.

A.why_wrong: Dutch has the second-lowest estimate (about 49%), but English is lower (about 39%).

B.why_wrong: Icelandic has one of the highest estimates (about 77%), not the lowest.

C.why_wrong: French works have an estimated survival of about 54%, higher than both English and Dutch.

sources.what: Kestemont, Karsdorp, de Bruijn, Driscoll, Kapitan, Ó Macháin, Sawyer, Sleiderink and Chao 2022, Science 375:765-769, 'Forgotten books: The application of unseen species models to the survival of culture': unseen species models from ecology applied to medieval chivalric and heroic narratives (e.g., romances about King Arthur) in Dutch, English, French, German, Icelandic and Irish; losses from library fires and recycled parchment; Table 1 survival ratios for works: Dutch 0.492, English 0.386, French 0.535, German 0.790, Icelandic 0.773, Irish 0.810
paper text (PDF) with Table 1
coverage: English works survive at about 38%, German, Irish and Icelandic above three-quarters; Dutch and French about half

items.notes: Values are the paper's Chao1 point estimates for works (not documents). Many works survive in a single document (326 singletons among 799 works). Subject replaced: mammal sleep totals (judge tell: trivial single-bar lookup dressed with an irrelevant Savage and West citation).

fixes: 'Mike Kestemont, Folgert Karsdorp, and colleagues' changed to 'Mike Kestemont and Folgert Karsdorp led a team that' (stock 'and colleagues' framing repeated across the file); 'gone unseen' changed to 'gone undetected' to keep the file's easy items at the official density

items.rewrite: New subject (estimated survival of medieval chivalric literature, Kestemont et al. 2022) replacing mammal sleep; the extreme asked for is the study's own headline contrast, and the cloned 'Although X ..., still lower than' frame is gone.

items.passage: Since its founding in 1966, the Duke Lemur Center in North Carolina has accumulated detailed records on nearly 4,200 strepsirrhine primates—the group comprising lemurs, lorises, and galagos—with longitudinal observations that frequently span an animal’s entire life. Drawing on these records, Sarah Zehr and colleagues compiled standardized life-history values, including adult body mass, gestation length, and activity pattern, for 27 taxa. Of the diurnal (day-active) taxa listed in the table, the one with the shortest expected gestation is the ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: red ruffed lemur, whose adults average about 3,600 grams.
gray mouse lemur, whose adults average about 80 grams.
eastern lesser bamboo lemur, whose adults average about 1,000 grams.
northern giant mouse lemur, whose adults average about 300 grams.

table.title: Life-History Values for Five Strepsirrhine Taxa at the Duke Lemur Center

items.explanation: Three taxa in the table are listed as diurnal: the eastern lesser bamboo lemur (145 days), the ring-tailed lemur (130 days), and the red ruffed lemur (98 days). The shortest of these expected gestations belongs to the red ruffed lemur, whose mean adult body mass is about 3,600 grams, so choice A completes the text.

B.why_wrong: The gray mouse lemur has the shortest expected gestation in the table (60 days), but it is nocturnal, not diurnal.

C.why_wrong: The eastern lesser bamboo lemur is the lightest of the diurnal taxa, but its expected gestation (145 days) is the longest of the three diurnal taxa, not the shortest.

D.why_wrong: The northern giant mouse lemur’s expected gestation (90 days) is shorter than the red ruffed lemur’s, but the northern giant mouse lemur is nocturnal.

sources.what: Zehr, Roach, Haring, Taylor, Cameron and Yoder 2014, Scientific Data 1:140019: since its establishment in 1966 the DLC has records for nearly 4,200 individuals from over 40 strepsirrhine taxa (lemurs, lorises and galagos); longitudinal data in many cases span an animal's entire life; life history table for 27 taxa

life history table values: mean adult body mass (both sexes) gray mouse lemur 82.65 g, northern giant mouse lemur 302.41 g, eastern lesser bamboo lemur 1012.49 g, ring-tailed lemur 2454.66 g, red ruffed lemur 3601.30 g; expected gestation 60, 90, 145, 130 and 98 days; activity N, N, D, D, D
Duke Lemur Center: located on the Duke University campus in Durham, North Carolina; established in 1966

items.notes: Activity pattern follows the dataset's two-way N/D coding (cathemeral taxa are coded D). Masses rounded to whole grams in the table and to round figures in the options. Subject replaced: early digital computers table (judge tell: encyclopedic history-of-computing table with no research source).
items.rewrite: New subject (Duke Lemur Center life-history data, Zehr et al. 2014) replacing early computers; filter-then-extreme kept, with a filter-ignoring distractor and a lightest-taxon distractor.

items.passage: Cigarette butts are the most commonly littered item in the world, and their filters, made of a plastic called cellulose acetate, can persist in the environment for years. RMIT University engineers Halil Kurmus and Abbas Mohajerani have tested one way of recycling this waste. They mixed butts into the clay used to manufacture fired bricks and then measured the bricks’ properties. The results revealed a trade-off: compared with control bricks containing no butts, bricks containing 1% butts by mass ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the claim?
options: had a lower thermal conductivity but also a lower compressive strength.
had a lower thermal conductivity and a higher compressive strength.
had a higher thermal conductivity but a lower dry density.
had a higher dry density but a lower compressive strength.

table.title: Properties of Fired Clay Bricks with and without Cigarette Butts

items.explanation: The table shows that the bricks with 1% butts had a lower thermal conductivity than the control bricks (0.898 versus 1.078), so they let less heat through, but also a lower compressive strength (30.8 versus 48.6 megapascals). Choice A states both comparisons correctly and shows the trade-off.

B.why_wrong: The bricks with butts had a lower compressive strength than the control bricks (30.8 versus 48.6 megapascals), not a higher one.

C.why_wrong: The bricks with butts had a lower thermal conductivity than the control bricks (0.898 versus 1.078), not a higher one.

D.why_wrong: The bricks with butts had a lower dry density than the control bricks (1,983 versus 2,114 kilograms per cubic meter), not a higher one.

sources.what: Kurmus and Mohajerani 2020, Materials 13(3):790, 'Recycling of Cigarette Butts in Fired Clay Bricks: A New Laboratory Investigation': CBs are the most commonly littered waste in the world; cellulose acetate filters with poor biodegradability can take many years to decompose; bricks with 0.5 to 2% CBs by mass tested against 0% control bricks; compressive strength 48.6 MPa (0%) vs 30.8 MPa (1%); dry density 2114 vs 1983 kg/m3; thermal conductivity 1.078 vs 0.898 W/mK
authors' affiliation: School of Engineering, RMIT University, Melbourne

items.notes: Subject replaced: Seikan and Channel tunnels (judge tell: generic engineering trivia with an irrelevant 'opened six years before' detail and a mechanical 2x2 grid). Options now pair different measures instead of a full larger/smaller factorial.
items.replaced: Galilean moons, Io vs Europa (duplicate of text_structure_and_purpose.S15_phenomenon_refute_two_third.hard)
items.rewrite: New subject (cigarette-butt fired clay bricks, Kurmus and Mohajerani 2020) replacing undersea tunnels; trade-off claim, options pair different measures rather than a 2x2 grid.

items.passage: Neglected vacant lots, common in many low-income urban neighborhoods, have been associated with depression among nearby residents. In a citywide trial in Philadelphia, physician Eugenia South and colleagues randomly assigned clusters of vacant lots to greening (trash removal, new grass and trees, and a low wooden fence), to trash cleanup alone, or to no intervention, and they surveyed nearby residents before and after the remediation. The type of intervention appeared to matter: ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: among residents near lots that received no intervention, the share who reported feeling worthless rose from about 7% to about 9%.
among residents near greened lots, the share who reported feeling worthless fell from about 10% to about 5%, whereas among residents near lots that were only cleaned of trash it changed little.
before the interventions, about 10% of residents near greened lots and about 10% of residents near trash-cleanup lots reported feeling worthless.
the share of residents who reported feeling worthless fell by about half near greened lots and by a similar amount near lots that received no intervention.

figure.title: Residents Reporting Feeling Worthless before and after Vacant-Lot Interventions
figure.description: Grouped bars for three study groups, each with a before bar (light gray) and an after bar (dark gray); y-axis 0 to 12 in steps of 2. No intervention: before 6.6, after 8.7. Trash cleanup only: before 9.7, after 9.2. Greening: before 10.3, after 5.1. Percentages are residents who said they had felt worthless less than half the time or more often in the past 30 days.

items.explanation: To show that the type of intervention mattered, the data must contrast greening with trash cleanup. The graph shows the share of residents near greened lots who reported feeling worthless dropping from about 10% to about 5%, while the share near trash-cleanup lots stayed near 9% to 10%. Choice B makes that comparison accurately.

A.why_wrong: The no-intervention values are read correctly, but they describe only the group that received no remediation, so they cannot show that one type of remediation worked better than the other.

C.why_wrong: Both groups were indeed near 10% before the interventions, but these are preintervention values, so they say nothing about the effect of either intervention.

D.why_wrong: The share near greened lots did fall by about half, but near lots with no intervention it rose, from about 7% to about 9%; it did not fall.

sources.what: South, Hohl, Kondo, MacDonald and Branas 2018, JAMA Network Open 1(3):e180298: citywide cluster randomized trial in Philadelphia, 110 vacant lot clusters assigned to greening (removing trash, grading, planting grass and a few trees, low wooden perimeter fence, monthly maintenance), trash cleanup, or no intervention; residents surveyed before and after; feelings of depression and worthlessness significantly decreased near greened lots

Table 2, all neighborhoods, worthless: no intervention 6.6% pre, 8.7% post; greening 10.3% pre, 5.1% post; trash cleanup 9.7% pre, 9.2% post; percentages are participants responding 'less than half the time' or more often in the past 30 days

neighborhood physical conditions including vacant or dilapidated spaces and trash are associated with depression (paper's introduction); Eugenia South, MD, Department of Emergency Medicine, University of Pennsylvania

items.notes: Graph shows unadjusted pre and post percentages from Table 2; the paper's significance tests compare each intervention with no intervention. Subject replaced: Finkenstaedt and Wolff word origins (judge tell: well-known internet chart; distractors simply misstated bar values).
items.rewrite: New subject (Philadelphia vacant-lot greening trial, South et al. 2018) replacing English word origins; distractors now true-but-irrelevant (control only, before only) and a half-true two-part option.

items.passage: In the central highlands of Mexico, smallholder farmers who grow maize landraces (traditional varieties adapted to local conditions) store seed from one season to the next in polypropylene woven bags, leaving it exposed to insects such as the maize weevil and the larger grain borer. Researchers at the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center, led by Sylvanus Odjo, compared this conventional practice with airtight hermetic containers, storing seed of four landraces in both types of storage for three or six months. Seed kept in woven bags sustained considerably more insect damage than seed of the same landrace kept hermetically over an equivalent storage period. For example, whereas Magdalena seed stored hermetically for six months had 1.2% insect damage, ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?
options: Magdalena seed stored in woven bags for three months had 3.5%.
VC Rosado seed stored in woven bags for six months had 61.4%.
Magdalena seed stored in woven bags for six months had 50.5%.
Magdalena seed stored hermetically for three months had 1.3%.

table.title: Insect Damage to Seed of Four Maize Landraces after Storage

items.explanation: The claim compares seed of the same landrace stored for the same length of time in the two kinds of storage. The example starts with Magdalena seed stored hermetically for six months (1.2%), so it must be completed with Magdalena seed stored in woven bags for six months, which the table shows had 50.5% insect damage. Only choice C matches both the landrace and the storage period.

A.why_wrong: This value is for Magdalena seed stored in woven bags for three months, not six, so it does not compare the two kinds of storage over the same period.

B.why_wrong: VC Rosado did have 61.4% damage after six months in woven bags, but the claim compares seed of the same landrace, and the example begins with Magdalena.

D.why_wrong: This value is also for hermetically stored Magdalena seed, after three months, so it compares two hermetic samples rather than woven bags with hermetic containers.

sources.what: Odjo, Bongianino, González Regalado et al. 2022, Insects 13(10):878, 'Effect of Storage Technologies on Postharvest Insect Pest Control and Seed Germination in Mexican Maize Landraces': central highlands of Mexico; smallholders store landrace seed in polypropylene woven bags (conventional practice), compared with hermetic containers (GrainPro hermetic bags or sealed plastic bottles); four landraces stored three and six months; pests Sitophilus zeamais and Prostephanus truncatus; lead author at CIMMYT

Table 2 insect damage (%): Magdalena 3.5 / 1.3 / 50.5 / 1.2; VC Amarillo 2.4 / 1.3 / 36.2 / 2.2; VC Rosado 38.1 / 4.1 / 61.4 / 2.4; SJR Azul 7.4 / 3.8 / 59.5 / 3.1 (3 months PP, 3 months HT, 6 months PP, 6 months HT)
common names: Sitophilus zeamais is the maize weevil; Prostephanus truncatus is the larger grain borer

items.notes: Hermetic containers were GrainPro bags for Magdalena and VC Amarillo and sealed PET bottles for VC Rosado and SJR Azul; the passage and table say 'hermetic container'. Values are means of three replicates. Subject replaced: alcohol and alkane boiling points (judge tell: chemistry textbook explanation; long passage for a trivial row lookup).

fixes: 'Sylvanus Odjo of the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center and colleagues' changed to 'Researchers at the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center, led by Sylvanus Odjo,' (stock 'and colleagues' framing); 'typically' dropped to stay at the skill's 119-word maximum

items.rewrite: New subject (hermetic vs woven-bag storage of Mexican maize landraces, Odjo et al. 2022) replacing alcohol/alkane boiling points; same-row matched comparison kept, distractors vary row, period and storage type.

items.passage: Although global sea level has risen throughout the past century, several tide gauges in southeastern Alaska record a persistent decline. Analyzing the gauge records, Christopher Larsen’s research group attributed this pattern to rapid uplift of the land itself: as glaciers have retreated since the end of the Little Ice Age, the underlying crust, relieved of the ice’s enormous weight, has been rebounding. Wherever such uplift outpaces the ocean’s rise, relative sea level (the height of the sea measured against the adjacent coastline) decreases. Between 1950 and 2010, for example, relative sea level at ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?
options: Grand Isle, Louisiana, fell by about 40 centimeters.
Ketchikan, Alaska, changed by only a few centimeters.
Juneau, Alaska, fell by more than 60 centimeters.
Sitka, Alaska, rose by about 10 centimeters.

figure.title: Change in Relative Sea Level at Four Tide Gauges since 1950
figure.y_axis: Change in annual mean relative sea level since 1950 (centimeters)
figure.description: Four lines at 1950, 1970, 1990 and 2010; y-axis −80 to 60 in steps of 20, with a heavier line at 0. Juneau, Alaska: 0, −24, −49, −72. Sitka, Alaska: 0, 0, −11, −9. Ketchikan, Alaska: 0, +1, −1, +2. Grand Isle, Louisiana: 0, +15, +36, +48. Juneau falls at every point; Grand Isle rises at every point; Ketchikan stays within a few centimeters of 0; Sitka ends about 9 centimeters lower.

items.explanation: The example must show relative sea level going down at a gauge in southeastern Alaska. The Juneau line falls at every point, ending about 72 centimeters below its 1950 level in 2010, so choice C completes the example.

A.why_wrong: Relative sea level at Grand Isle rose from 1950 to 2010, ending about 48 centimeters above its 1950 level; it did not fall.

B.why_wrong: Ketchikan’s line does stay within a few centimeters of its 1950 level, but a nearly unchanged sea level does not illustrate the decline the text describes.

D.why_wrong: Relative sea level at Sitka ended about 9 centimeters lower in 2010 than in 1950; it did not rise.

sources.what: NOAA Tides and Currents monthly mean sea level, Juneau 9452210, Sitka 9451600, Ketchikan 9450460, Grand Isle 8761724 (metric, relative to station MSL); annual means for 1950, 1970, 1990 and 2010 computed from monthly means
NOAA relative sea level trends: Juneau, Sitka and other southeast Alaska gauges negative; Grand Isle strongly positive

Larsen, Motyka, Freymueller, Echelmeyer and Ivins 2005, Earth and Planetary Science Letters 237:548-560, 'Rapid viscoelastic uplift in southeast Alaska caused by post-Little Ice Age glacial retreat' (uplift up to 32 mm/yr attributed to isostatic rebound after post-LIA ice loss)

glaciers thinned rapidly since the end of the Little Ice Age, unloading the crust and causing glacial isostatic rebound; Juneau has experienced a relative decrease in sea level; uplift about 15 mm/yr near Juneau
global mean sea level has risen over the past century

Larsen, Echelmeyer, Freymueller and Motyka 2003, JGR 108(B4), 'Tide gauge records of uplift along the northern Pacific-North American plate boundary, 1937 to 2001': relative sea level changes from tide gauge monthly means at 15 sites; the extremely rapid uplift is attributed entirely to viscoelastic postglacial rebound from tidewater-glacier retreat in Glacier Bay and regional post-Little Ice Age deglaciation (Crossref abstract)

items.notes: Graph values are changes in single-year annual means relative to 1950, rounded to whole centimeters, computed with Python from NOAA monthly means. Subject replaced: Sun Belt city populations (judge tell: textbook backstory with explanatory filler, structure cloned from the Singer item).

fixes: recomputed all 16 graph values from NOAA monthly means (annual means, change since 1950): all match after rounding (Juneau 0/−24/−49/−72, Sitka 0/0/−11/−9, Ketchikan 0/+1/−1/+2, Grand Isle 0/+15/+36/+48)
added Larsen et al. 2003 (JGR), the tide-gauge paper in which Larsen's group attributes the gauge-recorded uplift to post-Little Ice Age rebound
'Christopher Larsen and colleagues attributed' changed to 'Analyzing the gauge records, Christopher Larsen’s research group attributed' (stock 'and colleagues' framing)

items.rewrite: New subject (falling relative sea level in southeast Alaska from post-Little Ice Age uplift, Larsen et al. 2005, NOAA gauges) replacing Sun Belt city growth; true-but-irrelevant 'nearly unchanged' distractor added.

items.passage: Three species of brush-tailed penguins (genus Pygoscelis)—Adélie, chinstrap, and gentoo—breed on Signy Island in Antarctica’s South Orkney Islands. From nearly four decades of breeding-pair counts at regularly monitored colonies there, Michael Dunn and fellow researchers at the British Antarctic Survey found that the three species’ population trajectories differed considerably. Gentoos, for instance, increased substantially: in the study areas, the number of gentoo breeding pairs went from ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the assertion?
options: fewer than 500 in 1978–79 to more than 1,500 in 2013–14.
about 850 in 1999–2000 to about 670 in 2006–07.
fewer than 500 in 1978–79 to over 1,000 in 2013–14.

figure.title: Breeding Pairs of Three Penguin Species in Monitored Colonies on Signy Island, 1978–2014
figure.description: Three lines at the 1978–79, 1985–86, 1992–93, 1999–2000, 2006–07 and 2013–14 breeding seasons; y-axis 0 to 3,000 in steps of 250. Adélie (solid, triangles): 1,873; 2,787; 2,546; 1,313; 1,690; 1,731. Chinstrap (dashed, squares): 2,050; 2,219; 2,145; 1,440; 1,527; 1,417. Gentoo (dotted, circles): 370; 407; 536; 851; 668; 1,136. Gentoo starts below 500 and ends above 1,000, with a dip between 1999–2000 and 2006–07; chinstrap ends lower than it starts.

items.explanation: The text needs values showing the gentoo increase. The gentoo line starts at about 370 pairs in 1978–79, fewer than 500, and ends at about 1,140 pairs in 2013–14, over 1,000, so choice D completes the text accurately.

A.why_wrong: About 2,050 pairs in 1978–79 and about 1,400 in 2013–14 describe the chinstrap line, which fell; the gentoo line starts below 500.

B.why_wrong: Gentoo pairs did start below 500, but in 2013–14 they numbered about 1,140, not more than 1,500.

C.recipe: contradicts the claim (true data, wrong span)
C.why_wrong: The gentoo values for 1999–2000 (about 850) and 2006–07 (about 670) are read correctly, but they show a decline, so they cannot illustrate the gentoo increase.

sources.what: Dunn, Jackson, Adlard, Lynnes, Briggs, Fox and Waluda 2016, PLoS One 11(10): e0164025, 'Population Size and Decadal Trends of Three Penguin Species Nesting at Signy Island, South Orkney Islands': Adélie, chinstrap and gentoo; 38 years of annual counts from selected colonies plus decadal island-wide counts; gentoo pairs increased 255%, chinstrap declined 68%, Adélie declined 42% (whole island); lead author at the British Antarctic Survey
Pygoscelis is the genus of brush-tailed penguins (Adélie, chinstrap, gentoo)

items.passage: Laboratory experiments have suggested that painting one of a wind turbine’s three rotor blades black minimizes motion smear, the visual blurring that may prevent birds from detecting rotating blades in time to avoid them. Testing this prediction at the Smøla wind-power plant in Norway, Roel May and colleagues painted one blade black on each of four turbines in 2013. Trained dogs then searched for carcasses beneath those turbines and four unpainted control turbines, as they had since 2006. Painting was associated with reduced avian fatalities: ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: after the painting, searchers found 6 carcasses at the painted turbines, compared with 18 at the unpainted control turbines.
before the painting, searchers found 11 carcasses at the turbines that would later be painted, compared with 7 at the control turbines.
at the control turbines, searchers found 7 carcasses before the painting and 18 after it.
at the painted turbines, searchers found 11 carcasses before the painting and 18 after it.

figure.title: Bird Carcasses Found at Eight Turbines on Smøla before and after Painting
figure.description: Grouped bars for two periods, before painting (2006–2013) and after painting (2013–2016); legend: turbines with one blade painted black (dark gray) and unpainted control turbines (light gray). Y-axis 0 to 20 in steps of 2. Before painting: painted turbines 11, control turbines 7. After painting: painted turbines 6, control turbines 18. items.subtype: Data description (claim that holds across every part of a process)
items.passage: Because filter feeders such as oysters take in suspended particles as they feed, they are likely to swallow microplastics, the tiny plastic fragments that build up in the ocean. Rossana Sussarellu and colleagues exposed adult Pacific oysters (Crassostrea gigas) to polystyrene microspheres for two months while the oysters’ eggs and sperm were developing, then compared the oysters’ digestion and reproduction, as well as the growth of their larvae, with those of unexposed oysters. They concluded that the exposure harmed reproduction at each stage they examined, affecting eggs, sperm, and offspring alike.
items.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers’ conclusion?
options: For every measure in the table, the value for oysters exposed to microplastics was lower than the value for unexposed oysters.
Exposed females produced about 2.3 million eggs each, compared with about 3.8 million for unexposed females, and their eggs were about 1.6 micrometers smaller in diameter.
Compared with unexposed oysters, exposed oysters produced fewer and smaller eggs and slower-swimming sperm, and the larvae produced from their gametes had shorter shells at 17 days.
Exposed oysters absorbed a greater percentage of their algal food than unexposed oysters did, which suggests that the microplastics did not interfere with the oysters’ ability to feed.

table.title: Selected Measures for Pacific Oysters Exposed and Not Exposed to Microplastics
rows: Shell length of larvae at 17 days (micrometers)

items.explanation: The conclusion says the exposure harmed reproduction at each stage the team examined: eggs, sperm, and offspring. Exposed oysters had fewer eggs (2.3 versus 3.8 million) and smaller eggs (30.6 versus 32.2 micrometers), slower sperm (59.5 versus 77.5 micrometers per second), and larvae with shorter shells (227.5 versus 279.8 micrometers). Only choice C covers all three stages.

A.why_wrong: Absorption efficiency was higher for exposed oysters (51.8%) than for unexposed oysters (46.6%), so not every measure was lower.

B.why_wrong: The egg values are accurate, but they cover only one of the three stages; they say nothing about sperm or the larvae.

D.why_wrong: Absorption is read correctly, but it concerns feeding, not reproduction, so it cannot show that eggs, sperm, and offspring were all harmed.

items.subtype: Data description (passage criterion combined with the table)
items.passage: Plants native to ultramafic soils, which are naturally rich in nickel, sometimes concentrate the metal in their leaves. Botanists classify a species as a nickel hyperaccumulator if the dried leaves of at least some individuals contain more than 1,000 micrograms of nickel per gram (µg/g). Revising the classification of the Argophyllum species endemic to New Caledonia, Yohan Pillon and Vanessa Hequet measured the nickel in herbarium specimens of each species with a handheld X-ray spectrometer. Pillon and Hequet concluded that A. nitidum, the only species never found on ultramafic soils, is also the only one that does not qualify as a hyperaccumulator.
items.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support Pillon and Hequet’s conclusion?
options: A. montanum had the lowest median nickel content of the species in which nickel was detected, and it was also the only one of them whose highest value fell short of 1,000 µg/g.
Only A. ellipticum had a mean nickel content above 1,000 µg/g, and no nickel was detected in any of the A. nitidum specimens.
A. ellipticum had both the highest maximum and the highest mean nickel content of the five species in the table.
Every species in the table except A. nitidum had at least one specimen with more than 1,000 µg/g of nickel, whereas no nickel was detected in A. nitidum.

table.title: Leaf Nickel Content in Herbarium Specimens of Five Argophyllum Species

items.explanation: By the stated rule, a species qualifies if at least some individuals exceed 1,000 µg/g, so the highest value is the one to check. A. brevipetalum (1,675), A. ellipticum (6,670), A. montanum (1,110) and A. vernicosum (1,872) all have a specimen above 1,000 µg/g, while no nickel was detected in A. nitidum. Choice D states exactly this.

A.why_wrong: A. montanum’s highest value, 1,110 µg/g, is above 1,000 µg/g, so it does qualify as a hyperaccumulator.

B.why_wrong: The means are reported accurately, but the rule depends on whether some individuals exceed 1,000 µg/g, not on the average, so the option does not show that the other species qualify.

C.why_wrong: A. ellipticum does lead on both measures, but that says nothing about which species fall above or below the threshold.

items.subtype: Data description (effect that varies by group)
items.passage: Soil scientist John P. Reganold and his collaborators sampled strawberries from 13 pairs of side-by-side commercial fields near Watsonville, California, choosing each pair so that its organic and conventional fields shared the same soil type, microclimate, and strawberry variety. Besides measuring the berries’ mineral and antioxidant content, the team asked consumer panels, told as little as possible about the study’s purpose, to rate the berries’ overall acceptance and sweetness on a nine-point scale. The researchers concluded that whether consumers preferred organic strawberries depended on the variety: such a preference appeared for one of the three varieties sampled but not for the other two.
items.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers’ conclusion?
options: Consumers gave organic ‘Diamante’ strawberries an average overall acceptance rating of 6.09, compared with an average of 5.35 for conventional ‘Diamante’ strawberries.
Among the organically grown strawberries, ‘Lanai’ received the highest average ratings for both overall acceptance and sweetness, while ‘San Juan’ received the lowest average sweetness rating.
For each of the three varieties, organic strawberries received a higher average sweetness rating than conventional strawberries did, though the difference was greatest for ‘Diamante.’

Organic ‘Diamante’ strawberries outscored conventional ‘Diamante’ strawberries in both overall acceptance and sweetness, whereas for ‘Lanai’ and ‘San Juan’ the organic and conventional averages never differed by as much as 0.3 points.

table.title: Average Consumer Ratings of Organic and Conventional Strawberries (1–9 scale)

items.explanation: The conclusion has two parts: consumers preferred organic berries of one variety, and they did not prefer organic berries of the other two. Organic ‘Diamante’ berries beat conventional ones on both measures (6.09 versus 5.35 and 5.56 versus 4.73), while for ‘Lanai’ and ‘San Juan’ the organic and conventional averages were within 0.27 points of each other. Only choice D covers both parts.

A.why_wrong: The ‘Diamante’ comparison is accurate, but by itself it cannot show that the preference was absent for the other two varieties, which is the second half of the conclusion.

B.why_wrong: These comparisons among organic berries are accurate, but they compare varieties with one another instead of comparing organic with conventional berries of the same variety.

C.why_wrong: Organic ‘San Juan’ berries were rated less sweet (5.52) than conventional ‘San Juan’ berries (5.74).
